e: In preparation for a drought predicted by the Papua New Guinea National Weather Service, the cabinet approves money to be given to provinces of Papua New Guinea that may have already been affected.

The Conservation Environment and Protection Authority (CEPA), a government organization dedicated to sustainability and conservation of nature, begins developing Papua New Guinea's National Chemicals Management Strategy. This is being done with support from the Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme as well as the United Nations Environment Programme.
PNG and New Zealand Defence Ministers Elias Kapavore and Chris Penk sign an agreement to boost bilateral defence cooperation in Port Moresby.
Two passenger vessels sink en route from the Duke of York Islands to Kokopo, killing 27 of 29 passengers aboard both ships.
The government announces it will close Taiwan's representative office in Port Moresby as part of a move to strengthen relations with China.
Politician Theonila Roka Matbob wins the 2026 Goldman Environmental Prize.

The government tightens security at military bases and imposes movement restrictions after a group of soldiers sets up roadblocks in Port Moresby to protest alleged irregularities in army recruitment linked to former defence minister Billy Joseph, who is under investigation.
Soldiers block several roads across Port Moresby, protesting the military's recent recruitment controversies.
